text:
Carolina won this one the way the numbers said it should, even though the first period got away from them. Montreal scored three times in the opening 13 minutes, one of them a Nick Suzuki snap shot that carried a 6 percent chance of going in, and the Hurricanes still came out of the period tied on the shot clock and ahead in chances. They had out-chanced MTL 1.37 to 0.84 in expected goals over those 20 minutes, and they were down 3-2 anyway.

The second period settled it. CAR piled up 1.63 expected goals to MTL's 0.35, and the scoreboard finally caught up: Sebastian Aho tied it on the power play at 3:56, then Mark Jankowski put CAR in front with a backhand at 13:24. Zachary Bolduc scored twice for MTL and Taylor Hall twice for CAR, which is how they landed as the second and first stars. Aho added two assists, and his line was on the ice for 2.52 expected goals for against 0.7 against. Taylor Hall's second goal came at 12:21 of the third and made it 5-3, and Juraj Slafkovský pulled MTL within one at 16:57, only for Andrei Svechnikov to answer at 18:45 on a high-quality look (87 percent).

Over the full game, CAR held a 68-38 edge in shot attempts and 4.92 to 2.41 in expected goals, which works out to a team that wins this game 73 percent of the time on replay. Neither goalie had a good night. Brandon Bussi allowed 1.6 goals more than the shots against him warranted, and Jakub Dobes was 1.19 below expected as well. The difference was that CAR created far more chances than it gave up.
